{{Short description|American physicist (1943–2023)}}
{{like resume|date=August 2018}}

'''Richard Magee Osgood Jr.''' (December 28, 1943 – October 20, 2023) was an American applied and pure physicist ([[Condensed matter physics|condensed matter]] and [[chemical physics]] of surfaces, [[laser]] technology, [[Nanophotonics|nano-optics]]). He was Higgins Professor of Electrical Engineering<ref name="Richard M. Osgood Jr">[http://www.ee.columbia.edu/richard-osgood Richard M. Osgood Jr.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190622105425/http://www.ee.columbia.edu/richard-osgood |date=2019-06-22 }} on ee.columbia.edu</ref> and Applied Physics<ref>[http://apam.columbia.edu/richard-m-osgood-jr Richard M. Osgood, Jr.] on apam.columbia.edu</ref> at [[Columbia University]].

== Life and career ==
Richard Magee Osgood Jr. was born on December 28, 1943.<ref>data on People of the American Men and Women of Science, Thomson Gale 2004</ref> He began his scientific career in 1966, after graduating from the [[United States Military Academy|U.S. Military Academy]] with a bachelor's degree in 1965. He obtained a master's degree in 1968 from the [[Ohio State University]]. In 1973 he graduated from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] Ph.D. in physics. From 1973 to 1981, he then was on the scientific staff of [[MIT Lincoln Laboratory]]. In 1981 he was appointed to the faculty of Columbia University and in 1988 he was made "Higgins Professor"<ref name="Richard M. Osgood Jr"/> at Columbia University. From 1984 to 1990, he served as Co-Director of the Columbia Radiation Laboratory<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bnl.gov/bnlweb/pubaf/pr/2000/bnlpr071200.html |title=BNL press release |website=www.bnl.gov |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020225041031/http://www.bnl.gov/bnlweb/pubaf/pr/2000/bnlpr071200.html |archive-date=2002-02-25}} </ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://apam.columbia.edu/osgood-appointed-radiation-lab-co-director|title = Osgood Appointed Radiation Lab Co-Director|date = 28 April 2017}}</ref> and in 1986 was founder and until 1990 director of the Microelectronics Sciences Laboratories (MSL) at Columbia University.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://apam.columbia.edu/osgood-group-hot-bed-research|title=The Osgood Group, A Hot-Bed of Research|date=28 April 2017}}</ref>

In 1980 he served on the "Ad Hoc" [[United States Department of Energy|U.S. Department of Energy]] Committee for laser isotope separation. From 1984 to 2001 he was an advisor to the Laser and Laser and Chemistry Divisions of [[Los Alamos National Laboratory|Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory]].<ref>{{Cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WRqdAgAAQBAJ&q=Los+Alamos+Scientific+Laboratory+osgood&pg=PA93 | title=Avoiding Surprise in an Era of Global Technology Advances| isbn=978-0-309-09605-8| date=July 2005| publisher=National Academies Press}}</ref> From 1985 to 2002, he was on the advisory board of the Defense Advanced Research Project Agency ([[DARPA]] Defense Sciences Research Council). From 2000 to 2002 he served as associate director of the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] (Basic Energy Sciences Directorate)<ref>[http://www.bnl.gov/bnlweb/pubaf/pr/2000/bnlpr071200.html Richard Osgood Jr. Named Head of Brookhaven Lab1s Basic Energy Sciences] on bnl.gov, July 12, 2000</ref> and in 2002 Acting Director of the Nanoscience Centre. During this period DOE agreed to build the [[Center for Functional Nanomaterials]] at Brookhaven and the Department of [[Materials science|Materials Science]] was initiated. He was in the Basic Energy Sciences Advisory Board of the Department of Energy (DOE) in the mid-1980s.

Osgood was married to Alice (née Dyson) and had three children, Richard M. III, a physicist, Nathaniel D., a computer scientist, and Jennifer Smestad, an attorney. He also had six grandchildren. Richard M. Osgood Jr. died on October 20, 2023, at the age of 79.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Richard M. Osgood Jr. |url=https://www.west-point.org/users/usma1965/25536/ |website=West Point |access-date=30 October 2023}}</ref>

== Work ==
His research falls into two broad areas: 1. [[Condensed matter physics|Condensed matter]] and [[chemical physics]] studies of surfaces; 2. [[Optical physics]] and devices. Thus his research has included extensive studies in basic studies in optical-excited and -probed surface physics and chemistry, in the development of new infrared and UV lasers, optical physics, application of lasers for material processing.

His major research highlights are as follows.

He, along with William Eppers, developed the first high power CO laser<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Osgood | first1=R. M. | last2=Eppers | first2=W. C. | title=High Power CO–N<sub>2</sub>–He Laser | journal=Applied Physics Letters | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=13 | issue=12 | date=1968-12-15 | issn=0003-6951 | doi=10.1063/1.1652494 | pages=409–411| bibcode=1968ApPhL..13..409O }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Osgood | first1=R. | last2=Eppers | first2=W. | last3=Nichols | first3=E. | title=An investigation of the high-power CO laser | journal=IEEE Journal of Quantum Electronics | publisher=Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) | volume=6 | issue=3 | year=1970 | issn=0018-9197 | doi=10.1109/jqe.1970.1076425 | pages=145–154| bibcode=1970IJQE....6..145O }}</ref> (a [[Quantum cascade laser|quantum cascade]] [[gas laser]]), as well as other infrared lasers including the first high powered 16&nbsp;um laser for [[isotope separation]]. In 1979 he developed with Daniel Ehrlich and Peter Moulton a UV [[solid-state laser]], then the optically pumped solid-state laser with the shortest wavelength.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ehrlich | first1=D. J. | last2=Moulton | first2=P. F. | last3=Osgood | first3=R. M. | title=Ultraviolet solid-state Ce:YLF laser at 325 nm | journal=Optics Letters | publisher=The Optical Society | volume=4 | issue=6 | date=1979-06-01 | pages=184–6 | issn=0146-9592 | doi=10.1364/ol.4.000184 | pmid=19687843 | bibcode=1979OptL....4..184E }}</ref>

Osgood, along with [[Ali Javan]], made the first direct observation of vibrational-vibrational energy transfer and exchange in [[hydrogen halide]]s.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Osgood | first1=R.M. | last2=Javan | first2=A. | last3=Sackett | first3=P. B. | title=Measurement of Vibration-Vibration Energy Transfer Time in HF Gas | journal=Applied Physics Letters | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=20 | issue=12 | date=1972-06-15 | issn=0003-6951 | doi=10.1063/1.1654020 | pages=469–472| bibcode=1972ApPhL..20..469O }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ernst | first1=K. | last2=Osgood | first2=R.M. | last3=Javan | first3=A. | last4=Sackett | first4=P.B. | title=Measurement of the vibrational-virbrational exchange time (v = 2) for DF Gas | journal=Chemical Physics Letters | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=23 | issue=4 | year=1973 | issn=0009-2614 | doi=10.1016/0009-2614(73)89027-x | pages=553–556| bibcode=1973CPL....23..553E }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Osgood | first1=R. M. | last2=Sackett | first2=P. B. | last3=Javan | first3=A. | title=Measurement of vibrational-vibrational exchange rates for excited vibrational levels (2≤v≤4) in hydrogen fluoride gas | journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=60 | issue=4 | date=1974-02-15 | issn=0021-9606 | doi=10.1063/1.1681220 | pages=1464–1480| doi-access=free }}</ref> Later he made the first direct observation (with Steven Brueck) of vibration energy flow in molecules in cryogenic liquids the studies.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Brueck | first1=S.R.J. | last2=Deutsch | first2=T.F. | last3=Osgood | first3=R.M. | title=Vibrational energy relaxation of CH<sub>3</sub>F dissolved in liquid O<sub>2</sub> and Ar | journal=Chemical Physics Letters | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=51 | issue=2 | year=1977 | issn=0009-2614 | doi=10.1016/0009-2614(77)80416-8 | pages=339–343| bibcode=1977CPL....51..339B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Brueck | first1=S. R. J. | last2=Osgood | first2=R. M. | title=Vibrational energy relaxation and exchange in liquid N<sub>2</sub>–CO–OCS mixtures | journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=68 | issue=11 | year=1978 | issn=0021-9606 | doi=10.1063/1.435652 | pages=4941–4949| bibcode=1978JChPh..68.4941B }}</ref> A notable results of this work was the observation of the extremely long (60s) lifetime of N2<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Brueck | first1=S.R.J. | last2=Osgood | first2=R.M. | title=Vibrational energy relaxation in liquid N<sub>2</sub>-CO mixtures | journal=Chemical Physics Letters | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=39 | issue=3 | year=1976 | issn=0009-2614 | doi=10.1016/0009-2614(76)80331-4 | pages=568–572| bibcode=1976CPL....39..568B }}</ref> in its cryogenic state.

In the late 1970s, he, along with [[Thomas F. Deutsch]] and [[Daniel J. Ehrlich]],<ref name=volume38>{{cite journal | last1=Ehrlich | first1=D. J. | last2=Osgood | first2=R. M. | last3=Deutsch | first3=T. F. | title=Laser chemical technique for rapid direct writing of surface relief in silicon | journal=Applied Physics Letters | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=38 | issue=12 | date=1981-06-15 | issn=0003-6951 | doi=10.1063/1.92228 | pages=1018–1020| bibcode=1981ApPhL..38.1018E }}</ref><ref name=volume16>{{cite journal | last1=Ehrlich | first1=D. | last2=Osgood | first2=R. | last3=Deutsch | first3=T. | title=Laser microphotochemistry for use in solid-state electronics | journal=IEEE Journal of Quantum Electronics | publisher=Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) | volume=16 | issue=11 | year=1980 | issn=0018-9197 | doi=10.1109/jqe.1980.1070386 | pages=1233–1243| bibcode=1980IJQE...16.1233E }}</ref><ref name=volume35>{{cite journal | last1=Deutsch | first1=T. F. | last2=Ehrlich | first2=D. J. | last3=Osgood | first3=R. M. | title=Laser photodeposition of metal films with microscopic features | journal=Applied Physics Letters | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=35 | issue=2 | date=1979-07-15 | issn=0003-6951 | doi=10.1063/1.91026 | pages=175–177| bibcode=1979ApPhL..35..175D }}</ref><ref name=volume21>{{cite journal | last1=Ehrlich | first1=D. J. | last2=Osgood | first2=R. M. | last3=Deutsch | first3=T. F. | title=Photodeposition of metal films with ultraviolet laser light | journal=Journal of Vacuum Science and Technology | publisher=American Vacuum Society | volume=21 | issue=1 | year=1982 | issn=0022-5355 | doi=10.1116/1.571724 | pages=23–32| bibcode=1982JVST...21...23E }}</ref> demonstrated submicrometer-scale chemical processing of the surfaces of electronic materials.<ref>K. Ibbs, R. M. Osgood Jr., eds., Laser Chemical Processing for Microelectronics (Cambridge, 1988)</ref> These experiments demonstrated deposition of metals, etching of semiconductors, and [[Doping (semiconductor)|doping of semiconductors]]. One these methods, laser-induced Si etching<ref name="volume38"/> with micrometer resolution with an argon-[[ion laser]], which heated the surface and induced chemical reactions in a chlorine gas or [[hydrogen chloride]] gas atmosphere,<ref name=volume38 /> was later commercialized by Revise, a US semiconductor equipment company founded by Daniel Ehrlich and Kenneth Nill. He and his collaborators also developed techniques for producing spatially defined thin metal films with laser-induced [[photodissociation]].<ref name=volume16 /><ref name=volume35/><ref name=volume21/>

His work on use of laser micro- (and same cases nano-) chemistry for the processing of electronic materials led to his research examining the fundamental physics and chemistry of laser microchemistry, including the nature of the photodissociation in adsorbed films,<ref name="N. Camillone, III 2001">{{cite journal | last1=Camillone | first1=Nicholas | last2=Khan | first2=Khalid A. | last3=Yarmoff | first3=Jory A. | last4=Osgood | first4=Richard M. | title=Surface-Reconstruction-Switched Adsorbate Photofragmentation Dynamics | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=87 | issue=5 | date=2001-07-11 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.87.056101 | article-number=056101| pmid=11497789 | bibcode=2001PhRvL..87e6101C }}</ref><ref name="M. Camillone, III 2001"/><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Yang | first1=Q. Y. | last2=Schwarz | first2=W. N. | last3=Lasky | first3=P. J. | last4=Hood | first4=S. C. | last5=Loo | first5=N. M. | title=Highly anisotropic angular dependence of CH<sub>3</sub> fragmentation from electron-transfer reactions on CH<sub>3</sub>Br/GaAs(110) | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=72 | issue=19 | date=1994-05-09 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.72.3068 | pages=3068–3071| pmid=10056059 | bibcode=1994PhRvL..72.3068Y }}</ref> interactions in orienting surface species.

From 1998 to 2014 he and Miguel Levy developed ion-based "lift-off" methods for single-crystalline thin films, for example, ion-implantation of He to generate (Crystal Ion Slicing) slicing of metal-oxide films (garnets<ref name="M. Levy, R. M 1997"/><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Levy | first1=M. | last2=Osgood | first2=R. M. | last3=Liu | first3=R. | last4=Cross | first4=L. E. | last5=Cargill | first5=G. S. | last6=Kumar | first6=A. | last7=Bakhru | first7=H. | title=Fabrication of single-crystal lithium niobate films by crystal ion slicing | journal=Applied Physics Letters | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=73 | issue=16 | date=1998-10-19 | issn=0003-6951 | doi=10.1063/1.121801 | pages=2293–2295| bibcode=1998ApPhL..73.2293L }}</ref> and ferroelectrics). These garnet thin films were shown to be useful for [[optical isolator]]s.

In 2001, he, along with Mike Steel, developed novel [[photonic crystal]] fibers (photonic crystal fibers, PCF) with an elliptical cavity shape of the tubes<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Steel | first1=M. J. | last2=Osgood | first2=R. M. | title=Elliptical-hole photonic crystal fibers | journal=Optics Letters | publisher=The Optical Society | volume=26 | issue=4 | date=2001-02-15 | pages=229–31 | issn=0146-9592 | doi=10.1364/ol.26.000229 | pmid=18033556 | bibcode=2001OptL...26..229S }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Steel | first1=M.J. | last2=Osgood | first2=R.M. | title=Polarization and dispersive properties of elliptical-hole photonic crystal fibers | journal=Journal of Lightwave Technology | publisher=Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) | volume=19 | issue=4 | year=2001 | issn=0733-8724 | doi=10.1109/50.920847 | pages=495–503| bibcode=2001JLwT...19..495S }}</ref> and features such as high [[birefringence]] with a stable single-mode operation (zero walk off).

In 2002 he pioneered in developing Si photonics wires on silicon on insulator for new compact passive, active, and optical new linear device.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Osgood, Jr. | first1=R. M. | last2=Panoiu | first2=N. C. | last3=Dadap | first3=J. I. | last4=Liu | first4=Xiaoping | last5=Chen | first5=Xiaogang | last6=Hsieh | first6=I-Wei | last7=Dulkeith | first7=E. | last8=Green | first8=W. M. | last9=Vlasov | first9=Y. A. | title=Engineering nonlinearities in nanoscale optical systems: physics and applications in dispersion-engineered silicon nanophotonic wires | journal=Advances in Optics and Photonics | publisher=The Optical Society | volume=1 | issue=1 | date=2009-01-01 | issn=1943-8206 | doi=10.1364/aop.1.000162 | pages=162–235| bibcode=2009AdOP....1..162O |doi-access=}}</ref> His work in nonlinear Si photonics with his students and Jerry Dadap and Nicolae Panoiu is described in this reference. His group carried out the initial studies of linear and nonlinear Si-nanowire-photonics, including in 2001 [[Raman amplification]] ([[optical amplifier]]) in SOI technology ([[Silicon on insulator|silicon-on-insulator]], that is, silicon wires on an insulating underlay, with dimensions in the sub-micron range)<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Espinola | first1=Richard L. | last2=Dadap | first2=Jerry I. | last3=Osgood, Jr. | first3=Richard M. | last4=McNab | first4=Sharee J. | last5=Vlasov | first5=Yurii A. | title=Raman amplification in ultrasmall silicon-on-insulator wire waveguides | journal=Optics Express | publisher=The Optical Society | volume=12 | issue=16 | year=2004 | pages=3713–8 | issn=1094-4087 | doi=10.1364/opex.12.003713 | pmid=19483903 | bibcode=2004OExpr..12.3713E |doi-access=free}}</ref> In addition, he developed a high-speed Si thermooptical switch and demonstrated diode-pumped fourwave mixing in the waveguides.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Espinola | first1=R.L. | last2=Tsai | first2=M.C. | last3=Yardley | first3=J.T. | last4=Osgood | first4=R.M. | title=Fast and low-power thermooptic switch on thin silicon-on-insulator | journal=IEEE Photonics Technology Letters | publisher=Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) | volume=15 | issue=10 | year=2003 | issn=1041-1135 | doi=10.1109/lpt.2003.818246 | pages=1366–1368| bibcode=2003IPTL...15.1366E | s2cid=43914613 }}</ref> In later work, he, along with students and colleagues at IBM Watson Lab, demonstrated the first high gain [[optical parametric oscillator]] using an optically pumped Si-wire waveguide.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Liu | first1=Xiaoping | last2=Osgood | first2=Richard M. | last3=Vlasov | first3=Yurii A. | last4=Green | first4=William M. J. | title=Mid-infrared optical parametric amplifier using silicon nanophotonic waveguides | journal=Nature Photonics | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=4 | issue=8 | date=2010-05-23 | issn=1749-4885 | doi=10.1038/nphoton.2010.119 | pages=557–560|arxiv=1001.1533| bibcode=2010NaPho...4..557L | s2cid=119267295 }}</ref> This device operated above the [[two-photon absorption]] threshold and thus was not impaired by this nonlinear-loss mechanism.

His research into Si wire [[waveguide]]s, as well as his earlier work on III-V waveguide devices, led to a major effort to develop a more effective integrated optics design tool that was commonly available at the time.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Scarmozzino | first1=R. | last2=Osgood | first2=R. M. | title=Comparison of finite-difference and Fourier-transform solutions of the parabolic wave equation with emphasis on integrated-optics applications | journal=Journal of the Optical Society of America A | publisher=The Optical Society | volume=8 | issue=5 | date=1991-05-01 | issn=1084-7529 | doi=10.1364/josaa.8.000724 | page=724| bibcode=1991JOSAA...8..724S }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ilic | first1=I. | last2=Scarmozzino | first2=R. | last3=Osgood | first3=R.M. | title=Investigation of the Pade approximant-based wide-angle beam propagation method for accurate modeling of waveguiding circuits | journal=Journal of Lightwave Technology | publisher=Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) | volume=14 | issue=12 | year=1996 | issn=0733-8724 | doi=10.1109/50.545802 | pages=2813–2822| bibcode=1996JLwT...14.2813I }}</ref> The computational optical simulation work led to the founding of RSoft by Robert Scarmozzino, a major integrated optical simulation company.

In 2005, he, along with Steve Brueck, Nicholae Panoiu, S. Zhang, and W. Fan, demonstrated with the first observation of near infrared.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Zhang | first1=Shuang | last2=Fan | first2=Wenjun | last3=Panoiu | first3=N. C. | last4=Malloy | first4=K. J. | last5=Osgood | first5=R. M. | last6=Brueck | first6=S. R. J. | title=Experimental Demonstration of Near-Infrared Negative-Index Metamaterials | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=95 | issue=13 | date=2005-09-23 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.95.137404 | article-number=137404| pmid=16197179 | arxiv=physics/0504208 | bibcode=2005PhRvL..95m7404Z | s2cid=15246675 | url=http://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/142189/1/142189.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Zhang | first1=Shuang | last2=Fan | first2=Wenjun | last3=Malloy | first3=K. M. | title=Near-infrared double negative metamaterials | journal=Optics Express | publisher=The Optical Society | volume=13 | issue=13 | year=2005 | pages=4922–30 | issn=1094-4087 | doi=10.1364/opex.13.004922 | pmid=19498480 | bibcode=2005OExpr..13.4922Z |doi-access=free}}</ref> [[Negative index metamaterials|negative refractive index metamaterials]].

His research in light interactions with surfaces and this crystal layers led to a series of important experiments showing the role of surface dipoles to orient molecules for anisotropic photo- and electron fragmentation and the importance of coverage in controlling the fragmentation mechanism of surface bound molecules in the presence of UV illuminations, and finally (as mentioned earlier) the role of surface plasmons in enhancing and localizing surface photoreactions. In addition, his research using two-photon photoemission with pulsed UV lasers was instrumental in early studies of image states on vicinal single-crystal metal surfaces.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Smadici | first1=Serban | last2=Mocuta | first2=Dan | last3=Osgood | first3=Richard M. | title=Lateral motion of image-state electrons for metal-adsorbate regions on stepped metal substrates | journal=Physical Review B | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=69 | issue=3 | date=2004-01-29 | issn=1098-0121 | doi=10.1103/physrevb.69.035415 | article-number=035415| bibcode=2004PhRvB..69c5415S }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Smadici | first1=Serban | last2=Osgood | first2=Richard M. | title=Image-state electron scattering on flat Ag/Pt(111) and stepped Ag/Pt(997) metal surfaces | journal=Physical Review B | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=71 | issue=16 | date=2005-04-19 | issn=1098-0121 | doi=10.1103/physrevb.71.165424 | article-number=165424| bibcode=2005PhRvB..71p5424S }}</ref><ref>R. M. Osgood Jr. and X. Wang, "Image States on Single-Crystal Metal Surfaces." Chapter in Solid State Physics, H. Ehrenreich and F. Spaepen, eds., (Academic Press, 1998)</ref>
More recently in collaboration with Kevin Knox, Wencan Jin, Po-chun Yeh, Nader Zaki and Jerry Dadap, he used tightly focused UV photoemission based on a SPE-LEEM system to carry out the first photoemission studies of exfoliated [[graphene]] and [[transition metal]] dichalogide single samples and the influence of surface corrugation and layer number on sample electronic structure.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Jin | first1=Wencan | last2=Yeh | first2=Po-Chun | last3=Zaki | first3=Nader | last4=Zhang | first4=Datong | last5=Sadowski | first5=Jerzy T. | last6=Al-Mahboob | first6=Abdullah | last7=van der Zande | first7=Arend M. | last8=Chenet | first8=Daniel A. | last9=Dadap | first9=Jerry I. |author10-link=Irving P. As of November 11, 2015, Osgood's publications have been cited 13,696 times, and he has an [[h-index]] of 65.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Richard M Osgood Jr - Google Scholar Citations|url = https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=PtjsiWsAAAAJ&hl=en|website = scholar.google.com|access-date = 2015-11-12}}</ref>

== Awards ==
While at MIT, he was awarded a [[Hertz Foundation]] Predoctoral Fellowship.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://hertzfoundation.org/dx/fellows/fellows.aspx |title=Hertz Foundation Fellows |website=hertzfoundation.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110926144604/http://www.hertzfoundation.org/dx/fellows/fellows.aspx |archive-date=2011-09-26}} </ref> In 1989, he was awarded John Simon Guggenheim Fellowship<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/richard-m-osgood-jr/|title = John Simon Guggenheim Foundation {{pipe}} Richard M. Osgood Jr}}</ref> for studies in Light Surface Interactions.

In 1969 he received the Samuel Burka Award<ref>{{Cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3sT5BQAAQBAJ&q=Samuel+Burka+Award+osgood&pg=PT290 |title = Strength and Drive: The West Point Class of 1965|isbn = 978-1-4969-5731-3|last1 = Doughty|first1 = Robert A.|date = 2014-12-18| publisher=AuthorHouse }}</ref> of the US Avionics Laboratory<ref>[[Robert A. Doughty]]: Strength and Drive. The West Point Class of 1965. 2014, {{ISBN|978-1-4969-5732-0}}, [https://books.google.com/books?id=RWfrBQAAQBAJ&dq=%22Samuel+Burka+Award%22+Osgood&pg=PA260 p. 260]</ref> and the 1991 [[R. W. Wood Prize]].<ref>[http://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/rwwood/ R. W. Wood Prize] on osa.org</ref> He was a Fellow of the [[Optical Society]],<ref>[https://www.ll.mit.edu/about/fellows.html Professional Society Fellows] on ll.mit.edu</ref> the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]]<ref>IEEE Membership Directory. 1995, [https://books.google.com/books?id=WgNTAAAAMAAJ&q=%22Osgood+Richard%22+1943 p. 262]</ref> and the [[American Physical Society]] (APS).<ref>[http://www.aps.org/units/dcp/fellowship/index.cfm?year=1997 APS Fellowship] on aps.org</ref>

1991 to 1993 he was Distinguished Traveling Lecturer of the APS and 1986-1987 for IEEE CLEO and he was Plenary Speaker at the OITDA (Japanese Optoelectronic Industry and Technology Development Association).

1981 to 1988 he was Associate Editor of the IEEE Journal of Quantum Electronics and was on the editorial advisory board of the Springer Series in Materials Science.
